prompt:
Some people believe that when employers choose between candidates for a job, personal qualities such as reliability and the ability to work with others matter more than qualifications and experience.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?
instruction_line: You should spend about 40 minutes on this task. Write at least 250 words.
key_points: The task expects a clear position: agree / disagree / partly agree
The core claim is a comparison: are personal qualities more important than qualifications and experience — it is not enough to simply say both are necessary
At least two reasons plus a concrete example: technical knowledge can be taught on the job, while reliability and the ability to get along with others cannot easily be taught
A brief concession to the opposing view is expected: in some jobs, certification and experience are a matter of safety or legal requirement, and personal qualities are also subjective to measure
The stance must be restated clearly at the end; if arguing 'it depends on the job', it should explain which factor matters more in which jobs
common_mistakes: Skipping the comparison and simply listing the qualities of a good employee
Saying 'both are important' without stating a stance
Staying in abstract generalisations without giving a concrete work example
